Derive one piece of information from CPR numbers

Source: R/cpr_vectors.R
cpr_birth_date.Rd

Vector versions of the selections in add_cpr_info(): a vector of CPR numbers in, one vector of the same length out. They belong inside dplyr::mutate(), dplyr::filter() or ifelse(), where a data frame function does not fit.

Usage

cpr_birth_date(x)

cpr_birth_year(x)

cpr_sex(x)

cpr_valid(x)

cpr_mod11(x)

Arguments

x

A vector of CPR numbers. Values are read after the same cleaning as clean_cpr(), so dashes, spaces and a lost leading zero do not matter. Numeric vectors and factors are converted with as.character().

Value

A vector of the same length as x, without names.

Details

The values are exactly those of the matching selection in add_cpr_info(), from the same native code:

FunctionSelectionType
cpr_birth_date()bdayDate
cpr_birth_year()byearinteger
cpr_sex()sexinteger, 1 male (odd final digit), 0 female
cpr_valid()validlogical, never NA
cpr_mod11()mod11logical, NA when not ten digits

Birth date, birth year and sex are NA where cpr_valid() is FALSE. cpr_valid() checks ten digits and a real encoded date, not whether the number was assigned to a person; modulus 11 is not part of it, because the CPR office has issued numbers that fail it since 2007.

Birth year is its own function rather than an option of cpr_birth_date(), so each function always returns one type.

Each call parses the CPR numbers again. That costs little, about a tenth of a second per million values, but when you need several columns, add_cpr_info() parses once for all of them.

For age, see cpr_age().

See also

cpr_age(), add_cpr_info()

Examples

x <- c("0101004007", "111111-1118", "101004007", "3102004007", NA)
cpr_birth_date(x)
#> [1] "2000-01-01" "1911-11-11" "2000-01-01" NA           NA          
cpr_birth_year(x)
#> [1] 2000 1911 2000   NA   NA
cpr_sex(x)
#> [1]  1  0  1 NA NA
cpr_valid(x)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE
cpr_mod11(x)
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE    NA

# Typical use
# df |>
#   dplyr::filter(cpr_valid(pnr)) |>
#   dplyr::mutate(koen = ifelse(cpr_sex(pnr) == 1L, "Mand", "Kvinde"))
